Admittedly, this was not my initial idea. Originally, I was aiming to reimagine SCP-727 (Hephaestus' Forge) into a Lazarus Pit-type of device for CotBG worshippers. And then, I could not just let a generic character use the alt!SCP-727 and thought about the mechanical implants on Cain… And then, Cain pretty much highjacked his way to take centre stage.

In any case, I regret having to use a more popular SCP as the basis.

item.content:encoded:
If I have to drone in on semantics (and largely in my defence), the term "Church" usually connotes Christianity. And with a name like "Church of the Broken God", one would logically assume a wee bit of Christian favour in it (Okay, that is largely my headcanon and I believe that all words and names have meaning in context. Also, I'm not sure if those who coined the term thought of it as such, but there's always headcanon.).

That said, I do admit that the parallels between my article and the Christian story are rather uncanny. But then again, the SCPs involved are Biblical entities.

P.S. I'm not making up the connotations part, even Dictionary.com says so.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm… not convinced.

Indeed, it's an attractive re-imagining. But the whole story feels kinda mashed together at some points, and deserving of a more in-depth exploration of the universe where it exists. Is this an Unfounded-compatible tale? Is this an incarnation of the Foundation posing as the Church of the Broken God (and thus making a horribad job of actual containment)? Is this a corrupt Church altogether?

The messianic concept also drips a bit too much of a messiah according to the Christian archetype. A human mother that is impregnated through divine act and will, thus gives birth to a little bundle of reality-defying skills who grows up to die fighting a traitorous enemy and then is brought back by a mourning father; true, it might be Qabil playing history to his benefit, but it makes me feel a bit too detracted from the story. It's a story I've read before, after all.

Otherwise, the writing feels solid to me, and the Conspectus format remains the best goi_format in this site; you could have played a bit more with the footnotes, but all in all, it's a good doc. I'm torn. I'll come back before the voting period is over, but for now, no-vote.
